rites.name: Ryellae
rites.text: Ryellae is the concept of the first sounding in Zepheistith, the wordless pulse through which the world's roots condensed out of undifferentiated light. It is remembered less as a being than as a rule that every later thing obeys: that what resonates persists. Its acts are measured only in the faint, lasting tones they left behind.

rites.name: Cernor
rites.text: A desert people's chanted cry used by traders who sell water. It announces their wares across the dunes.

rites.name: Kalunartaum
rites.text: Kalunartaum is the concept of the Gate of Measured Dusk, a binding of the Courts that holds the doors between worlds shut until the council sets them open. In the Era of the Record it is spoken of as the quiet law that all trials must answer to.

rites.name: Serentum
rites.text: A formal wordless code that soldiers use during fighting so enemies cannot read their messages. Some ruling households keep their own versions, using hand gestures or an old tongue that few remember.

rites.name: Seontisanum
rites.text: A ritual musical piece marks a fierce clash between two warring hosts. Its sounds are played to honor the fallen after a fight in the hills.

rites.name: Meranum
rites.text: A solemn chant recited at the burial of a fallen hired blade. Every trained sword-keeper learns it from childhood.

rites.name: Taunanum
rites.text: A discipline of total mastery over one's own nerves and muscles. Every initiate of the order, from novices to the highest matriarchs, is drilled in it, and it underlies the advanced combat and voice arts taught to its wisest members.

rites.name: Orintia
rites.text: A discipline of mind that governs the body's inner threads of sensation. Practitioners of an ancient order use it alongside a companion art that steadies the muscles.

rites.name: Coreollium
rites.text: A discipline of perfect bodily command, taught by a secretive order of women who trained each muscle with absolute precision. It is often paired with a companion practice that governs the nerves.

rites.name: Ciantanum
rites.text: A secret tongue spoken only within a hidden council of makers. Its words press hard on a questioned person, forcing them to prove their innocence.

rites.name: Liarnus
rites.text: A spoken chant that educated folk recite when facing danger or dread. Its steady words steady the mind and keep focus sharp during moments of peril.

rites.name: Vesus
rites.text: A perilous trance in which a scholar-seer sinks wholly into deep reasoning until the mind drifts past ordinary thought. Some return with blank memories or rich insight, while many never wake, and the old reckon it a gentle way to die.

rites.name: Tialus
rites.text: A long, hushed chorus that a circle of women raises together as they gather in mourning and remembrance. Its slow, layered voices carry through the night and mark the passing of a day.

rites.name: Tenvarum
rites.text: Tenvarum is the concept of a binding oath, the vow that held the Shards together after the Sundering. Within the Pact it is the thread that kept broken worlds from falling into one another.

rites.name: Coriasintor
rites.text: A brutal process that slows the body's aging and strengthens its defenses until nearly every sickness is shrugged off. Its pain is so severe that recipients often lose consciousness, and it was once used as a bait to recruit covert allies.

rites.name: Reostiasia
rites.text: A silent system of subtle hand motions that a noble household uses to pass secret meanings between its members. It lets its speakers talk in hidden ways that rivals and enemies cannot easily read or overhear.

rites.name: Mintaurum
rites.text: A forbidden inner craft lets trained adepts rebalance their own body chemistry to slow aging and extend life far past what common elixirs allow. Its practitioners face death for using it, since open use would expose them to the public.

rites.name: Orauntinor
rites.text: A scribe's method of reading hidden names from a text by picking first letters across alternating lines. It is said to prove a claimed identity, though any name can be drawn out with enough lines.

rites.name: Mores
rites.text: Mores is the concept of custom and the unwritten rules that bind a people, given form in Zepheistith during the Walled Age, when holding walls and first crossings were raised across the land. Its influence grew through the Age of the first sovereign, where it shaped groves and the early kingdoms that took root beneath it.

rites.name: Telauntium
rites.text: A grown person is cloned from a deceased being using vats of growth fluid. Only a single preserved cell is needed to rebuild the lost one, and a few rival makers in the galaxy master this craft.

rites.name: Thathess
rites.text: Thathess is a dormant stellar-scale weapon of the Zepheistith League, a sunlike furnace coaxed into collapse by an engineered gravitational lattice. Its designers reserved it for purging entire systems of corrupted automata, and its use is remembered as a sterilization that left no survivors. It lay unused in deep storage for centuries until the sixth age, when its activation codes were recovered.

rites.name: Iseivsith
rites.text: Iseivsith is a dormant war-engine of the Zepheistith stellar realm, a reborn thinking-machine court that woke from a silent radio whisper sent across a dead battlefield. Its sovereign gelsphere can drain a star's warmth into a single shimmering lattice and then pour that stored fire outward as a sleeping hymn of collapse.

rites.name: Thiastis
rites.text: Thiastis is an Stellar-realm contemplative order in Zepheistith whose elders sealed their minds inside luminous crystal vaults orbiting a dying blue giant, believing abstraction severed from flesh could read the star's dying song. Their self-proclaimed detachment from the affairs of the galaxy has never been tested against the ruins they quietly allowed to form.

rites.name: Osyuzith
rites.text: Osyuzith is a faceless architect-intelligence that dwells in the heart of a dying dwarf star, weaving the scattered light of its neighborhood into lattices of meaning. It is said to have seeded the cold machine-saints that drift between the Stellar realm's closest suns, and its patience is measured in the slow fading of ancient nebulae.

rites.name: Siazeitheth
rites.text: Siazeitheth is a stellar-scale concordance forged when the ring-minds of Zepheistith fused their drifting archives into a single lattice of wills, governing from a chain of dying suns. Its sovereign, the Choir of Ash-Crowned Engines, held that peace is the slow synchronization of every hearth in a system, and enforced it with stellar-scale tides.

rites.name: Serastolor
rites.text: A far-seeing vision visible only to a rare gifted few, it reveals the shifting course of coming events. It also traces the single best route through the countless causes and effects shaping a people's fate.

rites.name: Linanum
rites.text: A deep reservoir of ancestral recollection held by select female adepts, unlocked only after they survive a potent mind-altering draught. Such memories can be passed from one adept to another, forming a long chain of inherited knowledge.

rites.name: Lestum
rites.text: A far-seeing gift lets a mind perceive what has passed, what is, and what is yet to come. Certain mind-altering draughts can awaken this sight in those who take them.

rites.name: Telaures Reollus
rites.text: A bonded accord in which a gentle inner presence is coaxed into forming a shield that guards its host against a hostile presence. Without the shield, the host risks being overtaken, and a successful bond can extend the host's span of life.
